Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e9e3d31d2c141af15518ce6578ef26480fe97878 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2016 19:21:56 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] Allow 16M send/recv blocks

Fix an off by one error introduced by fcff0f3 which triggers an
assertion when 16M blocks are used with send/recv.  This fix was
intentionally not folder in to the Illumos commit so it can be
easily cherry-picked by upstream.

Signed-off-by: Brian Behlendorf <behlendorf1@llnl.gov>

diff --git a/module/zfs/bqueue.c b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
index 1ddc697b5..89655cf53 100644
--- a/module/zfs/bqueue.c
+++ b/module/zfs/bqueue.c
@@ -69,7 +69,7 @@ void
 bqueue_enqueue(bqueue_t *q, void *data, uint64_t item_size)
 {
 	ASSERT3U(item_size, >, 0);
-	ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
 	mutex_enter(&q->bq_lock);
 	obj2node(q, data)->bqn_size = item_size;
 	while (q->bq_size + item_size > q->bq_maxsize) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `module/zfs/bqueue.c`**
   - The assertion check for `item_size` was modified from:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
     ```
   - This change allows `item_size` to be equal to `q->bq_maxsize`, fixing an off-by-one error that was causing an assertion failure when using 16M blocks with send/recv operations.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bqueue.c` directly addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified as `fcff0f3`). The change ensures that the maximum size of the queue (`bq_maxsize`) can accommodate blocks of size 16M without triggering an assertion failure. This fix is crucial for maintaining the functionality of the system when handling large data blocks, thereby improving the robustness of the send/recv operations.

Reason:
The assertion incorrectly enforced that `item_size` must be strictly less than `bq_maxsize`, which prevented the maximum allowed size (16M) from being enqueued. This caused an assertion failure when attempting to enqueue a block of that size.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	ASSERT3U(item_size, <=, q->bq_maxsize);
```
Reason:
The fix changes the assertion to allow `item_size` to be equal to `bq_maxsize`, thus enabling the use of the maximum allowed size (16M) without triggering an assertion failure.
